SCOPE This Regulation applies to the emission of gaseous pollutants from positive-ignition engines of vehicles of categories L3, L4 and L5. 1/ <u>1/ As defined in Annex 7 to the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3) (document</u> TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.1/Amend.2 as last amended by Amend.4). 1 2. DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Regulation, 2.1. "Approval of a vehicle" means the approval of a vehicle type with regard to the limitation of the emission of gaseous pollutants from the engine; 2.2. "Vehicle type" means a category of power-driven vehicles which do not differ in such essential respects as: 2.2.1. the equivalent inertia determined in relation to the reference weight as prescribed in annex 4, paragraph 5.2., to this Regulation, and 2.2.2. the engine and vehicle characteristics as defined in annex 1, items 1-6 and 8, and annex 2 to this Regulation; 2.3. "Reference weight" means the weight of the vehicle in running ordery increased by a uniform figure of 75 kg. The weight of the vehicle in running order is its total unladen weight with all tanks full; 2.4. “Engine crank-case" means the spaces in or external to an engine which are connected to the oil sump by internal or external ducts through which gases and vapours can escape; 2.5. "Gaseous pollutants" mean carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides, the last-named being expressed in nitrogen dioxide (NO2) equivalent.

title: APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL
text: APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL

heading: APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL
text: The application for approval of a vehicle type with regard to limitation of the emission of gaseous pollutants from its engine shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by his duly accredited representative.

heading: APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL
text: It shall be accompanied by the undermentioned documents in triplicate and the following particulars: 3.2.1. a description of the engine type comprising all the particulars shown in annex 1 to this Regulation; 3.2.2. particulars concerning the vehicle as shown in annex 2 to this Regulation.

heading: APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL
text: A vehicle representative of the vehicle type to be approved shall be submitted to the technical service responsible for conducting approval tests, for the tests referred to in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.

title: APPROVAL
text: APPROVAL

heading: APPROVAL
text: If the vehicle type submitted for approval pursuant to this Regulation meets the requirements of paragraphs 5. and 6. below, approval of that vehicle type shall be granted.

heading: APPROVAL
text: An approval number shall be assigned to each type approved, the first two digits (at present 01 corresponding to the 01 series of amendments which entered into force on 31 May 1988) shall indicate the highest number of the series of amendments incorporated in the Regulation at the time of issue of the approval. The same Contracting Party may not assign the same number to another vehicle type.

heading: APPROVAL
text: Notice of approval or of refusal of approval of a vehicle type pursuant to this Regulation shall be communicated to the Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation, by means of a form conforming to the model in annex 2 to this Regulation and of drawings and diagrams supplied by the applicant for approval, in a format not exceeding A 4 (210 x 297 mm) or folded to that format and on an appropriate scale.

heading: APPROVAL
text: There shall be affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, to every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under this Regulation an international approval mark consisting of: 4.4.1. a circle surrounding the letter “E” followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval; <u>2/</u> <u>2/ 1 for Germany, 2 for France, 3 for Italy, 4 for the Netherlands, 5 for Sweden, 6 for Belgium, 7 for Hungary, 8 for the Czech Republic, 9 for</u> Spain, 10 for Serbia and Montenegro, 11 for the United Kingdom, 12 for Austria, 13 for Luxembourg, 14 for Switzerland, 15 (vacant), 16 for Norway, 17 for Finland, 18 for Denmark, 19 for Romania, 20 for Poland, 21 for Portugal, 22 for the Russian Federation, 23 for Greece, 24 for Ireland, 25 for Croatia, 26 for Slovenia, 27 for Slovakia, 28 for Belarus, 29 for Estonia, 30 (vacant), 31 for Bosnia and Herzegovina, 32 for Latvia, 33 (vacant), 34 for Bulgaria, 35 (vacant), 36 for Lithuania, 37 for Turkey, 38 (vacant), 39 for Azerbaijan, 40 for The former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, 41 (vacant), 42 for the European Community (Approvals are granted by its Member States using their respective ECE symbol), 43 for Japan, 44 (vacant), 45 for Australia, 46 for Ukraine, 47 for South Africa, 48 for New Zealand, 49 for Cyprus, 50 for Malta, 51 for the Republic of Korea, 52 for Malaysia and 53 for Thailand. heading: APPROVAL
text: If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved, under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement, in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation, the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1. need not be repeated; in such a case the regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols of all the Regulations under which approval has been granted in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.

heading: APPROVAL
text: The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.

heading: APPROVAL
text: The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vertical data plate affixed by the manufacturer.

heading: APPROVAL
text: Annex 3 to this Regulation gives examples of arrangements of approval marks.

title: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS
text: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS
text: General The components liable to affect the emission of gaseous pollutants shall be so designed, constructed and assembled as to enable the vehicle in normal use, despite the vibration to which it may be subjected, to comply with the provisions of this Regulation.

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS
title: Description of tests
text: Description of tests

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: The vehicle shall be subjected, according to its category, to tests of two types, I and II, as specified below. 5.2.1.1. <u>Type-I test (verifying the average emission of gaseous pollutants in a congested urban area).</u>

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: The test shall be carried out by the method described in annex 4 to this Regulation. The gases shall be collected and analysed by the prescribed methods.

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: Subject to the provisions of paragraph 5.2.1.1.3. below, the test shall be repeated three times. In each test, the mass of the carbon monoxide, the mass of the hydrocarbons and the mass of the nitrogen oxides obtained shall be less, for a vehicle of given reference weight, than the amounts shown in the tables I and II to this Regulation. The measurement of the mass per km of nitrogen oxides is made for information only.

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: Nevertheless, for each of the pollutants rsferred to in the foregoing paragraph, one of the three results obtained may exceed by not more than 10 per cent the limit prescribed in that paragraph for the vehicle concerned, provided the arithmetical mean of the three results is below the prescribed limit. In cases where the prescribed limits are exceeded for more than one pollutant, it shall be immaterial whether this occurs in the same test or in different tests.

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: The number of tests prescribed in paragraph 5.2.1.1.2. above shall be reduced in the conditions hereinafter defined, where V1 is the result of the first test and V2 the result of the second test for each of the pollutants referred to in paragraph 5.2.1.1.2. of this Regulation.

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: Only one test shall be made if, for all pollutants concerned, V1 ≤ 0.70L.

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: Only two tests shall be made if, for all pollutants concerned, V1 ≤ 0.85L but for at least one of the pollutants V1 > 0.70L. In addition, for each of the pollutants concerned, V2 must satisfy the requirements that V1 + V2 < 1.70L and V2 < L. 5.2.1.2. <u>Type-II test (verifying the emission of carbon monoxide at idling speed).</u>

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: The carbon monoxide content of the exhaust gases emitted with the engine idling shall not exceed 4.5 per cent by volume.

heading: SPECIFICATIONS AND TESTS > Description of tests
text: Conformity with this requirement shall be checked by a test carried out by the method described in annex 5 to this Regulation.

title: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE

heading: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: Every modification of the vehicle type shall be notified to the administrative department which approved the vehicle type. The department may then either: 6.1.1. consider that the modifications made are unlikely to have an appreciable adverse effect and that in any case the vehicle still complies with the requirements; or 6.1.2. require a further test report from the technical service responsible for conducting the tests.

heading: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: Confirmation or refusal of approval, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 4.3. above to the Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation.

EXTENSION OF APPROVAL 7.1. <u>Vehicle types of different reference weights</u> Approval of a vehicle type may be extended to vehicle types which differ from the type approved only in respect of their reference weight, provided that the reference weight of the vehicle type for which extension of the approval is requested requires merely the use of the next higher or next lower equivalent inertia. 7.2. <u>Vehicle types with different over-all gear ratios</u>

heading: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: Approval granted to a vehicle type may under the following conditions be extended to vehicle types differing from the type approved only in respect of their over-all transmission ratios:

heading: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: For each of the transmission ratios used in the type-I test, it shall be necessary to determine the proportion where V2 and V1 are respectively the speed at 1000 r.p.m. of the engine of the vehicle type approved and the speed of the vehicle type for which extension of the approval is requested.

heading: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: If for each gear ratio E ≤ 8 per cent, the extension shall be granted without repeating the type-I tests.

heading: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: If for at least one gear ratio E > 8 per cent and if for each gear ratio E ≤ 13 per cent, the type-I tests shall be repeated, but may be performed in a laboratory chosen by the manufacturer subject to the approval of the Administration granting approval. The report of the tests shall be sent to the recognized laboratory. 7.3. <u>Vehicle types of different reference weights and different over-all transmission ratios</u> Approval granted to a vehicle type may be extended to vehicle types differing from the approved type only in respect of their reference weight and their over-all transmission ratios, provided that all the conditions prescribed in paragraphs 7.1. and 7.2. above are fulfilled. 7.4. <u>Three-wheeled vehicles</u> Approval granted to a two-wheeled vehicle type may be extended to three-wheeled vehicles using the same engine and exhaust system and using a transmission that is either the same or differs only in respect of the over-all transmission ratios.

heading: MODIFICATIONS OF THE VEHICLE TYPE
text: Restriction When a vehicle type has been approved in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs 7.1. to 7.4. above, such approval may not be extended to other vehicle types.

title: CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION

heading: CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: Every vehicle bearing an approval mark as prescribed under this Regulation shall conform, with regard to components affecting the emission of gaseous pollutants by the engine, to the vehicle type approved.

heading: CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: In order to verify conformity as prescribed in paragraph 8.1. above, a vehicle bearing the approval mark required by this Regulation shall be taken from the series.

heading: CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: As a general rule, conformity of the vehicle with the approved type shall be verified on the basis of the description given in the approval form and its annexes, and, if necessary, a vehicle shall be subjected to all or some of the tests of types I and II referred to in paragraph 5.2.above.

heading: CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: In a type-I test carried out on a vehicle taken from the series the mass of carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons obtained shall not exceed the limits prescribed for this category of vehicles in tables I and II. The measurement of the mass per km of nitrogen oxides is made for information only.

title: PENALTIES FOR NON-CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: PENALTIES FOR NON-CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION

heading: PENALTIES FOR NON-CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: The approval granted in respect of a vehicle type pursuant to this Regulation may be withdrawn if the requirements laid down in paragraph 8.1. are not complied with or if the vehicle or vehicles taken fail to pass the tests prescribed in paragraph 8.3. above.

heading: PENALTIES FOR NON-CONFORMITY OF PRODUCTION
text: If a Party to the Agreement applying this Regulation withdraws an approval it has previously granted, it shall forthwith so notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation, by means of a copy of the approval form bearing at the end, in large letters, the signed and dated annotation "APPROVAL WITHDRAWN”.

PRODUCTION DEFINITELY DISCONTINUED If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a type of motor cycle under this Regulation, he shall inform thereof the authority which granted the approval. Upon receiving the relevant communication that authority shall inform the other Parties to the Agreement which apply this Regulation thereof by means of a copy of the approval form bearing at the end, in large letters, the signed and dated annotation "PRODUCTION DISCONTINUED".

NAMES AND ADDRESSES OF TECHNICAL SERVICES RESPONSIBLE FOR CONDUCTING APPROVAL TESTS, AND OF ADMINISTRATIVE DEPARTMENTS The Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation shall communicate to the United Nations Secretariat the names and addresses of the technical services responsible for conducting approval tests and of the administrative departments which grant approval and to which forms certifying approval or refusal or withdrawal of approval, issued in other countries, are to be sent. <u>Table I LIMITS IN TERMS OF REFERENCE WEIGHT R FOR MOTOR CYCLES WITH TWO-STROKE</u> ENGINES

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST
text: INTRODUCTION This annex describes the procedure for the type-I test defined in paragraph 5.2.1.1. of this Regulation.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > (Verifying the average emission of gaseous pollutants in a congested urban area)
text: The vehicle shall be placed on a dynamometer bench equipped with a brake and fly-wheel. A test lasting a total of 13 minutes and comprising four cycles shall be carried out without interruption. Each cycle shall comprise 15 phases (idling, acceleration, steady speed, deceleration, etc.). During the test, the exhaust gases shall be diluted with air to obtain a constant volumetric flow of mixture. Throughout the test, from the mixture thus obtained, samples at a constant rate of flow shall be collected in a bag for successive determination of the concentration (average for the test) of carbon monoxide, unburnt hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > OPERATING CYCLE ON THE DYNAMOMETER BENCH > Use of the gearbox
text: During acceleration, the motor cycle shall be tested in whichever gear is appropriate to the acceleration imposed by the cycle. A higher gear shall be engaged at the latest when the rotating speed is equal to 110% of the speed corresponding to the maximum power of the eng ine. If a motor cycle reaches the speed of 20 km/h in first gear, or 35 km/h in second gear, the next (higher) gear shall be engaged at these speeds. In these cases no further gear shifts into higher gears shall be allowed. If, during the acceleration phase, the gear shifts have taken place at these fixed vehicle speeds, the following constant speed phase shall be performed in the gear which is engaged when the motor cycle enters that constant speed phase, regardless of the engine speed.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > OPERATING CYCLE ON THE DYNAMOMETER BENCH > Use of the gearbox
text: During deceleration, a lower gear shall be engaged either before the engine starts to idle roughly or when the engine revolutions are equal to 30% of the speed corresponding to the maximum power of the engine, whichever of these conditions is reached first. No change down to first gear shall be effected during deceleration.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > OPERATING CYCLE ON THE DYNAMOMETER BENCH > Use of the gearbox
text: Motor cycles equipped with automatic-shift gearboxes shall be tested with the highest gear (Drive) engaged. The accelerator shall be used in such a way as to obtain the steadiest possible acceleration at which the various gears can be engaged in the normal order. The tolerances prescribed in paragraph 2.4. shall apply. 2.4. <u>Tolerances</u>

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > OPERATING CYCLE ON THE DYNAMOMETER BENCH > Use of the gearbox
text: A tolerance of 1 km/h above or below the theoretical speed shall be allowed during all phases of the cycle. Speed tolerances greater than those prescribed shall be accepted during phase changes provided that the tolerances are never exceeded for more than 0.5 second on any occasion with the exception of the provisions of paragraphs 6.5.2. and 6.6.3. of this annex.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > OPERATING CYCLE ON THE DYNAMOMETER BENCH > Use of the gearbox
text: The time tolerance shall be ± 0.5 sec.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > OPERATING CYCLE ON THE DYNAMOMETER BENCH > Use of the gearbox
text: The speed and time tolerances shall be combined as indicated in appendix 1 to this annex.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > OPERATING CYCLE ON THE DYNAMOMETER BENCH > Use of the gearbox
text: The distance driven during the cycle shall be measured to ± 2 per cent.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > VEHICLE AND FUEL 3.1. <u>Test vehicle</u>
text: The vehicle shall be presented in good mechanical condition. It shall have been run in and have been driven at least 1,000 km before the test. The laboratory may decide if a vehicle which has been driven less than 1,000 km before the test should be accepted.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > VEHICLE AND FUEL 3.1. <u>Test vehicle</u>
text: The exhaust device shall not exhibit any leak likely to reduce the quantity of gas collected, which shall be the quantity emerging from the engine.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > VEHICLE AND FUEL 3.1. <u>Test vehicle</u>
text: The leakproofness of the intake system may be checked to ensure that carburation is not affected by an accidental intake of air.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > VEHICLE AND FUEL 3.1. <u>Test vehicle</u>
text: The settings of the vehicle shall be those prescribed by the manufacturer.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > VEHICLE AND FUEL 3.1. <u>Test vehicle</u>
text: The laboratory may verify that the vehicle conforms to the performances stated by the manufacturer, that it can be used for normal driving, and in particular that it is capable of starting when cold and when hot.

text: Motor fuel The fuel shall be the reference fuel whose specification's are given in annex 6 to this Regulation. If the engine is lubricated by mixture, the oil added to the reference fuel shall comply as to grade and quantity with the manufacturer's recommendations.

title: Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A simplified diagram of the collecting, diluting, sampling and volume-measuring equipment for use with the exhaust gases emitted during the test will be found in appendices 2 and 3 to this annex.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The testing equipment is described in the paragraphs which follow; each component is identified by the reference symbol used in the sketch in appendices 2 and 3. Different equipment may be used if, in the opinion of the Administration’s technical officers, it gives equivalent results.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A device for collecting all exhaust gases emitted during the test; it is generally an open type device, maintaining the atmospheric pressure at the motor cycle exhaust outlet(s). Nevertheless, if the back pressure conditions are complied with (< ±125 mm of H20), a closed system may be used. The gas collection shall be such that there is no condensation which could appreciably modify the nature of exhaust gases at the test temperature.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A pipe (Tu) linking the device and the gas-sampling equipment. The pipe and the device shall be made of stainless steel or of some other material which does not affect the composition of the gases collected and withstands their temperatures.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A heat exchanger (Sc) capable of limiting the temperature variation of the diluted gases in the pump intake to ±5 °C throughout the test. This exchanger (Sc) shall be equipped with a preheating system able to bring the exchanger to its operating temperature (with the tolerance of ± 5 °C) before the test begins.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A displacement pump P1 designed to draw in the diluted gases and actuated by a motor having several strictly constant speeds. The delivery shall be sufficient to ensure intake of the entire quantity of exhaust gas. A device using a critical-flow venturi tube may likewise be used.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A device continuously recording the temperature of the diluted gases entering the pump.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A probe, S3, mounted alongside the gas-collecting device, for sampling the diluent air at a constant rate throughout the test through a pump, a filter and a flow-metre.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A probe S2, directed upstream into the stream of diluted gases upstream of the displacement pump, for sampling the mixture or diluted gases at a constant rate throughout the test through a pump, a filter and a flowmetre. The minimum rate of flow of the stream of gas in the above two sampling systems shall be at least 150 l/h.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Two filters, F2 and F3, placed after probes S2 and S3 respectively for the purpose of trapping any solid particles suspended in the samples <u>en route to the collecting bags. Special care shall be taken that they do not</u> cause any charge of the concentrations of the gaseous components of the samples.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Two pumps, P2 and P3, whose purpose is to take samples through probes S2 and S3 respectively for collection in bags Sa and Sb.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Two manually adjustable valves, V2 and V3, mounted downstream of pumps P2 and P3 respectively to control the flow of the samples sent to the bags.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Two rotameters, R2 and R3, placed in series on the "probe, filter, pump, valve, bag" lines “S2, F2, P2, V2, Sa" and "S3, F3, P3, V3, Sb” respectively to provide an immediate visual check on the rate at which samples are being taken.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Sampling bags for the diluent air and the mixture of diluted gases, leakproof and of sufficient capacity not to hinder the normal flow of the samples. They shall have an automatic closure on the side of the bag and be able to be rapidly secured, and in such a way as to avoid leakage, either on the sampling circuit or on the measuring circuit at the end of the test.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Two differential pressure gauges, g1 and g2, placed as follows: g1 - before the pump P1, to determine the pressure shortfall below atmospheric pressure of the exhaust gas/diluent air mixture; g2 - before and after the pump P1, to evaluate the pressure increase induced in the gas stream.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: A cumulative counter CT to count the revolutions of the rotary displacement pump P1.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Three-way cocks on the above sampling circuits to direct the sample streams either to the outside or to their respective collecting bags throughout the test. The valves shall be quickacting. They shall be made of materials which do not affect the composition of the gases; furthermore, their flow sections and shapes shall be such as to minimize load losses so far as is technically possible. 4.3. <u>Analytical equipment</u>

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
title: Determining HC concentration
text: Determining HC concentration

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment > Determining HC concentration
text: The concentration of unburnt hydrocarbons (HC) in the samples collected in bags SA and SB during the tests shall be determined by means of a flame ionization analyser.

title: Determining CO and CO ~~2~~ <u>concentrations</u>

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment > Determining CO and CO ~~2~~ <u>concentrations</u>
text: The concentrations of carbon monoxide (C0) and carbon dioxide (CO2 ) in the samples collected in bags SA and SB during the tests shall be determined by means of an analyser of the non-dispersive type with absorption in the infrared.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
title: Determining NO X concentrations
text: Determining NO X concentrations

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment > Determining NO X concentrations
text: The concentrations of nitrogen oxides (NOX) in the samples collected in bags SA and SB during the tests shall be determined by means of a chemiluminescence analyser. 4.4. <u>Accuracy of instruments</u>

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: Since the brake is calibrated in a separate test, the accuracy of the dynamometer is not indicated. The total inertia of the rotating masses, including that of the rollers and the rotating part of the brake (see paragraph 5.2.), shall be given to within ± 2 per cent.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The speed of the vehicle shall be measured by the speed of rotation of the rollers connected to the brake and fly-wheels. It shall be measurable to within ± 2 km/h in the speed range 0-10 km/h and to within ± 1 km/h at speeds above 10 km/h.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The temperature considered in paragraph 4.2.2.5. shall be measurable to within ± 1 °C. The temperature considered in paragraph 6.1.1. shall be measurable to within ± 2 °C.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The atmospheric pressure shall be measurable to within ± 1 mm (mercury gauge).

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The degree to which the pressure of the diluted gases falls short of atmospheric pressure at the intake of pump P1 (see paragraph 4.2.2.12.) shall be measured to within ± 3 mm (mercury gauge). The difference in pressure of the diluted gases between the sections before and after pump P1 (see paragraph 4.2.2.13.) shall be measured to within ± 3 mm (mercury gauge).

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The volume displaced by each complete rotation of the pump P1 and the displacement value at the minimum feasible pumping speed, as recorded by the cumulative revolution counter CT, shall be such that the overall volume of the exhaust gas/diluent air mixture displaced by the pump P1 during the test can be determined to within ± 2 per cent.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The analysers shall have a measuring range compatible with the accuracy required to measure the content of the various constituents to within ± 3 per cent, disregarding the accuracy of the standard (calibration) gases. The flame ionization analysers used to determine the HC concentration shall be capable of reaching 90 per cent of full scale in less than one second.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > TEST EQUIPMENT > Gas-sampling and volume-measuring equipment
text: The content of the standard calibration gases shall not differ by more than ± 2 per cent from the reference value of each gas. The diluent shall be nitrogen.

title: Setting the brake
text: Setting the brake

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Setting the brake
text: The brake shall be so adjusted as to reproduce the operation of the vehicle on the level at a steady speed between 45 and 55 km/h.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Setting the brake
text: The brake shall be adjusted in the following manner:

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Setting the brake
text: An adjustable stop limiting the maximum speed to between 45 km/h and 55 km/h shall be mounted in the fuel-feed regulating device. The speed of the vehicle shall be measured by means of a precision speedometer or computed from the time measured over a given distance on a level, dry road, in both directions, with the stop applied. The measurements, which shall be repeated at least three times in both directions, shall be taken over a distance of at least 200 m and with a sufficiently long acceleration distance. The average speed shall be determined.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Setting the brake
text: Other systems for measuring the power needed to propel the vehicle (e.g. measuring the torque on the transmission, measuring of deceleration) shall also be accepted.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Setting the brake
text: The vehicle shall then be placed on the dynamometer bench and the brake so adjusted as to obtain the same speed as that reached in the road test (fuel-feed regulating device in stop position and same gear-box ratio). This brake setting shall be maintained throughout the test. After adjusting the brake, the stop in the feed device shall be removed.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Setting the brake
text: Adjustment of the brake on the basis of road tests may be performed only if the barometric pressure does not differ by more than ± 10 torr, nor the air temperature by more than ± 8 °C between the road and the space housing the dynamometer bench.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST
title: Conditioning of vehicle
text: Conditioning of vehicle

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Conditioning of vehicle
text: Before the test, the vehicle shall be stored at a temperature between 20° and 30°C. After the engine has been kept idling for 40 seconds, two complete cycles are effected without collecting exhaust gas.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Conditioning of vehicle
text: The tyre pressure shall be the same as that indicated by the manufacturer for the preliminary road test for brake adjustment. However, if the diameter of the rollers is less than 50 mm, the pressure in the tyres shall be increased by 30-50 per cent to prevent damage to them.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Conditioning of vehicle
text: The weight on the he driven wheel should be the same as the vehicle in normal driving conditions, with a driver weighting 75 kg. 5.4. <u>Adjustment of analytical apparatus</u>

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PREPARING THE TEST > Conditioning of vehicle
text: Calibration of analysers The quantity of gas at the indicated pressure compatible with the correct functioning of the equipment shall be injected into the analyser with the aid of the flow metre and the pressure reducing valve mounted on each gas cylinder. The apparatus shall be adjusted to indicate as a stabilized value the value inserted on the standard gas cylinder. Starting from the setting obtained with the gas cylinder of greatest capacity, a curve shall be drawn of the deviations of the apparatus according to the content of the various standard cylinders used. The flame ionization analyser shall be recalibrated periodically, at intervals of not more than one month, using air/propane or air/hexane mixtures with nominal hydrocarbon concentrations equal to 50 per cent and 90 per cent of full scale. Non-dispersive infrared absorption analysers shall be checked at the same intervals using nitrogen/C0 and nitrogen/CO2 mixtures in nominal concentrations equal to 10, 40, 60, 85 and 90 per cent of full scale. To calibrate the NOX chemiluminescence analyser, nitrogen/nitrogen oxide (NO) mixtures with nominal concentrations equal to 50 per cent and 90 per cent of full scale shall be used. The calibration of all three types of analysers shall be checked before each series of tests, using mixtures of the gases which are measured in a concentration equal to 80 per cent of full scale. A dilution device can be applied for diluting a 100 per cent calibration gas to required concentration.

title: Special conditions for carrying out the cycle
text: Special conditions for carrying out the cycle

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Special conditions for carrying out the cycle
text: The temperature in the room housing the roller-bed shall be between 20° and 30°C throughout the test and shall approximate as closely as possible to that of the room in which the vehicle has been conditioned for the test.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Special conditions for carrying out the cycle
text: The vehicle shall be approximately level during the test so as to avoid any abnormal distribution of the fuel.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Special conditions for carrying out the cycle
text: At the end of the first 40 second idling period (see paragraph 6.2.2.), a current of air of variable speed shall be blown over the vehicle. There will follow two complete cycles during which time no exhaust gas shall be collected. The blower shall incorporate a mechanism controlled by the speed of the bench roller so that, within the range 10-50 km/h, the initial linear wind speed is within 10 per cent of the relative speed of the roller. For roller speeds below 10 km/h the wind speed may be nil. The final section of the blower shall have the following characteristics: Area: at least 0.4 m2 ; Height of lower edge above the ground: between 0.15 and 0.20 m; Distance from the front of the vehicle: between 0.3 and 0.45 m.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Special conditions for carrying out the cycle
text: During the test, the speed shall be plotted against time so that the correctness of the cycles performed can be assessed.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Special conditions for carrying out the cycle
text: The temperatures of the cooling water and the crank-case oil may also be recorded.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
title: Starting up the engine
text: Starting up the engine

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Starting up the engine
text: After the preliminary operations on the equipment for collecting diluting, analysing and measuring the gases (see paragraph 7.1. below) have been carried out, the engine shall be stored up by means of the devices provided for the purpose - the choke, the starter valve, etc, - in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Starting up the engine
text: The engine shall be kept idling for a maximum period of 40 seconds. The first test cycle shall start at the same time as the beginning or the collection of samples and the measurements of the revolutions of the pump.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
text: Use of the manual choke The choke shall be cut out as soon as possible, and in principle before acceleration from zero to 50 km/h. If this principle cannot be applied the moment of effective cut-out shall be stated. The method used to adjust the choke shall be that indicated in the manufacturer's specifications.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
title: Idling
text: Idling

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling
title: Manual-sbift gear-box
text: Manual-sbift gear-box

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling > Manual-sbift gear-box
text: During periods of idling, the clutch shall be engaged and the gears in neutral.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling > Manual-sbift gear-box
text: To enable the accelerations to be performed according to the normal cycle, the vehicle shall be placed in first gear, with the clutch disengaged, 5 seconds before the acceleration following the idling period considered.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling > Manual-sbift gear-box
text: The first idling period at the beginning of the cycle shall consist of 6 seconds of idling in neutral with the clutch engaged and 5 seconds in first gear with the clutch disengaged.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling > Manual-sbift gear-box
text: For the idling periods in the middle of each cycle, the corresponding times shall be 16 seconds in neutral and 5 seconds in first gear with the clutch disengaged.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling > Manual-sbift gear-box
text: The last idling period in a cycle shall consist of 7 seconds in neutral with the clutch engaged.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling
text: Semi-automatic-shift gear-boxes The manufacturer’s instructions for driving in town or, in their absence, the rules applicable to manual-shift gearboxes shall be followed.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling
text: Automatic-shift gear-boxes The selector shall not be operated at any time during the test unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise. In the latter case the procedure prescribed for manual-shift gear-boxes shall be applied. 6.5. <u>Accelerations</u>

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling
text: Accelerations shall be so performed that the rate of acceleration is as constant as possible throughout the phase.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Idling
text: If the acceleration capability of the motor cycle is not sufficient to carry out the acceleration phases within the prescribed limits of tolerances, the motor cycle shall be driven with the throttle fully open, until the speed prescribed for the cycle is reached and the cycle shall be normally carried on.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
title: Decelerations
text: Decelerations

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Decelerations
text: All decelerations shall be effected by fully closing the accelerator, the clutch remaining engaged. The clutch shall be disengaged at a speed of 10 km/h.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Decelerations
text: If the period of deceleration is longer than that prescribed for the corresponding phase, the vehicle's brakes shall be used to enable the timing of the cycle to be maintained.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Decelerations
text: If the period of deceleration is shorter than that prescribed for the correponding phase, the timing of the theoretical cycle shall be restored by a constant speed or idling period merging into succeeding constant speed or idling operation. In that case, paragraph 2.4.3. to this annex is not applicable.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Decelerations
text: At the end of the deceleration period (halt of the vehicle on the rollers), the gears shall be placed in neutral and the clutch engaged.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
title: Steady speeds
text: Steady speeds

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Steady speeds
text: “Pumping” or the closing of the throttle shall be avoided when passing from acceleration to the succeeding steady speed.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Steady speeds
text: Periods of constant speed shall be achieved by keeping the accelerator position fixed.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST
text: PROCEDURE FOR SAMPLING, ANALYSIS AND VOLUMETRIC MEASUREMENT OF EMISSIONS 7.7.1. 0perations prior to starting the vehicle

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Steady speeds
text: The sample-collecting bags SA and SB shall be emptied and closed.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Steady speeds
text: The rotary displacement pump P1 shall be started without the revolution counter.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Steady speeds
text: Sampling-pumps P2 and P3 shall be started with the switching valves set for discharge into the atmosphere; valves V2 and V3 shall be used to adjust the flow.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Steady speeds
text: The temperature sensing device T and the pressure gauges g1 and g2 shall be brought into operation.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Steady speeds
text: The pump revolution counter CT and the roller revolution counter shall be set at zero.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
title: Start of samplng and volumetric measurement operations
text: Start of samplng and volumetric measurement operations

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Start of samplng and volumetric measurement operations
text: After 40 seconds' preliminary unladen idling and two preparatory cycles (initial moment of the first cycle), the operations specified in paragraphs 7.2.2. to 7.2.5. below shall be carried out strictly simultaneously.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Start of samplng and volumetric measurement operations
text: The switching valves shall be set for collection in bags SA and SB of the samples which are still being taken by probes S2 and S3, and which have hiterto been discharged into the atmosphere.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Start of samplng and volumetric measurement operations
text: The moment of starting the test shall be marked on the graphs of the analogue recorders connected to the temperature sensing devices T and the differential pressure gauges g1 and g2.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Start of samplng and volumetric measurement operations
text: The cumulative revolution counter CT shall be engaged with the pump P1.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > Start of samplng and volumetric measurement operations
text: The blower referred to in paragraph 6.1.3. shall be started.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
title: End of sampling, and volumetric measurement operations
text: End of sampling, and volumetric measurement operations

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > End of sampling, and volumetric measurement operations
text: The operations specified in paragraphs 7.3.2. to 7.3.5. below shall be carried out strictly simultaneously at the end of the fourth test cycle.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > End of sampling, and volumetric measurement operations
text: The switching valves shall be set to close off bags SA and SB and to discharge into the atmosphere the samples taken by pumps P2 and P3 through probes S2 and S3.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > End of sampling, and volumetric measurement operations
text: The moment of ending the test shall be marked on the graphs of the analogue recorders (see paragraph 7.2.3.).

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > End of sampling, and volumetric measurement operations
text: The cumulative revolution counter CT shall be disengaged from the pump P1.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS > End of sampling, and volumetric measurement operations
text: The blower referred to in paragraph 6.1.3. shall be switched off. 7.4. <u>Analysis of the samples contained in the bags</u> The analysis shall begin as soon as possible, and in any event not later than 20 minutes after the end of the tests, in order to determine: The concentrationc of hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide in the sample of diluent air contained in bag SB; The concentrations of hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide in the sample of diluted exhaust gases contained in bag SA.

heading: Annex 4 TYPE-I TEST > PROCEDURE FOR BENCH TESTS
text: Measuring the distance covered The distance S actually covered shall be arrived at by multiplying the number of revolutions read from the cumulative counter (see paragraph 4.1.l.) by the circumference of the roller. This distance shall be measured in km.

text: INTRODUCTION This annex describes the procedure for the type-II test defined in paragraph 5.2.1.2 of this Regulation.

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST
title: CONDITIONS OF MEASUREMENT
text: CONDITIONS OF MEASUREMENT

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST > CONDITIONS OF MEASUREMENT
text: The fuel shall be the reference fuel whose specifications are given in annex 6 to this Regulation.

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST > CONDITIONS OF MEASUREMENT
text: The content by volume of carbon monoxide shall be measured immediately after the type-I test, with the engine at idling speed.

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST > CONDITIONS OF MEASUREMENT
text: In the case of vehicles with manually operated or semi-automaticshift gear-boxes, the test shall be carried out with the gear lever in the "neutral" position and with the clutch engaged.

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST > CONDITIONS OF MEASUREMENT
text: In the case of vehicles with automatic-shift gear-boxes, the test shall be carried out with the gear selector in either the "neutral" or the "parking” position.

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST
title: SAMPLING OF EXHAUST GASES
text: SAMPLING OF EXHAUST GASES

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST > SAMPLING OF EXHAUST GASES
text: The exhaust outlets shall be provided with an air-tight extension, so that the sample probe used to collect exhaust gases may be inserted into the exhaust outlet at least 60 cm, without increasing the back pressure of more than 125 mm H20, and without disturbance of the vehicle running. The shape of this extension shall however be chosen in order to avoid, at the location of the sample probe, any appreciable dilution of exhaust gases in the air. Where a motor cycle is equipped with an exhaust system having multiple outlets, either these shall be joined to a common pipe or the content of carbon monoxide must be collected from each of them, the result of the measurement being reached from the arithmetical average of these contents.

heading: Annex 5 TYPE-II TEST > SAMPLING OF EXHAUST GASES
text: The concentrations in CO (CCO) and CO2 (CCO2 ) shall be determined from the measuring instrument readings or recordings, by use of appropriate calibration curves.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: This annex describes the method to be used to determine the power absorbed, as measured on the road by a dynamometric brake. The power absorbed comprises, as measured on the road, the power absorbed by frictiona1 effects and the power absorbed by the power-absorption device. The dynamometer is brought into operation beyond the range of test speeds. The device used for starting up the dynamometer is then disconnected from the dynamometer, and the rotational speed of the roller or rollers decreases. The kinetic energy of the device is dissipated by the power absorption unit of the dynamometer and by the frictional effects of the dynamometer. This method disregards variations in the roller’s interna1 frictional effects caused by the rotating mass of the vehicle. The difference between the stopping time of the free rear roller and that of the front drive roller can be disregarded in the case of two-roller dynamometers. The following procedures will be used:

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Measure the rotational speed of the roller if this has not already been done. A fifth wheel, a revolution counter or some other method may be used.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Place the vehicle on the dynamometer or devise some other method of starting up the dynamometer.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Use the fly~wheel or any other system of inertia simulation for the vehicle-mass category most commonly used with the dynamometer.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Bring the dynamometer to a speed of 50 km/h.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Note the power absorbed.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Bring the dynamometer to a speed of 60 km/h.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Disconnect the device used to start up the dynamometer.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Note the time taken by the dynamometer to pass from a speed of 55 km/h to a speed of 45 km/h.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
text: Set the power-absorption device at a different level.

heading: Annex 7 METHOD OF DETERMINING THE POWER ABSORBED ON THE ROAD BY THE DYNAMOMETRIC BRAKE FOR MOTOR CYCLES
